title: fix: keep Activity permission errors stable during refresh
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Activity briefly replaces a settled permission error with loading placeholders when unrelated sessions change.

## User Impact

User impact: denied Activity views remain stable during automatic refresh, while Retry, changed filters, reconnection and relevant access changes can still refresh them. Existing rows remain visible during a same-query refresh and are cleared if the response denies access.

This does not grant new access or introduce a limited-readable-person view. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Activity now treats a permission denial as settled for the current selection rather than retrying it for unrelated activity. Explicit retries and authority changes bypass that settled state. Hidden-tab authority updates wait for visibility, and superseded responses cannot restore old rows.

## Evidence

Maintainer verification on `09087a32dfc6a609d56147cd59304c63882ca805`: 58 owner/page tests and both browser scenarios passed. In the isolated real Gateway run, an unrelated session event left the settled denial at one request, one alert and zero skeletons; Retry made a new request. The separate held-response browser scenario retained the accepted row during refresh and removed it on denial. Restoring only the prior production owner/page files made two selected cases fail, including four unwanted reads instead of one. The candidate was restored byte-for-byte; no production changes were needed.

- Production-bundle Chromium regressions fail on base `ecaefd29e7f1a23657de41a7eb217ba083c477be` and pass on candidate `2902a87bcc9fb29ac8033772fd225862f7b6072a`.
- Held-response browser proof: an unrelated session event increased denied Activity reads from one to two and showed loading placeholders before the fix; after the fix there is still one read and the permission error stays visible. Clicking Retry recovers to rows. A subsequent held refresh retains the same row element, then removes it when access is denied.
- Isolated real-Gateway proof: a synthetic guest receives a real permission denial for another synthetic person’s Activity. Creating an unrelated session produces a real session-change event without retrying the denied view. Clicking Retry still makes one new request.
- Both browser regressions pass on candidate `2902a87bcc9fb29ac8033772fd225862f7b6072a`; 58 focused tests pass, plus a separate consumer run with 36 unit and five browser-component tests (overlapping coverage).
- UI typecheck, targeted lint/format, test-line budget and diff checks pass.
- Canonical local autoreview reported no P0–P2 findings against the pinned base, on a local snapshot verified identical to this candidate. The reviewer did not execute tests independently and lacked some unchanged lifecycle context; a separate complete-source parent review covered the owner, page state, changed tests, real-Gateway test and refresh coordinator and found no actionable issue. Local ClawSweeper was unavailable. [Hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196939#issuecomment-6783601301) completed with one actionable P3 test-port finding; the follow-up uses the existing claimed Gateway port-block lifecycle instead of releasing an ephemeral port before startup.

The initial published head `5a3c0bfe68065a23bd6413bc6bf99b61eec87e33` adds only publication metadata to candidate `2902a87bcc9fb29ac8033772fd225862f7b6072a`; those commits have the same Git tree. Follow-up `f697d42197cfeb0f6c61fef61ae7212a22ba400b` changes only test-fixture lifecycle and its exact eight-line test-budget allocation, not production behavior. The corrected real-Gateway regression passes (9.7 seconds; 56.4-second invocation), with a clean Gateway shutdown and Chromium exit. All four existing Gateway port-ownership tests and seven selected state-acquisition rollback cases pass. A fresh canonical review of the follow-up and complete fixture/claim owners found no P0–P3 issues or material source-context gaps; the reviewer did not independently run tests. Published head `09087a32dfc6a609d56147cd59304c63882ca805` adds only publication metadata to this follow-up and has the same Git tree. No CI result is claimed.

### Before

An unrelated session update replaces the settled denial with loading placeholders.

![Before: Activity denial replaced by loading placeholders](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9bbae4c7-efc9-4d74-976c-049fb527eff5)

### After

The same update leaves the denial visible without another request. Retry remains available.

![After: Activity denial remains stable during an unrelated session update](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7e9e6e22-2196-4edb-9e51-3254d25dc023)

The real-Gateway test uses isolated synthetic state and the actual list authorization/event path. It does not invoke an inference model or modify a live service.

## Contributor credit

Reported and scoped with @vyctorbrzezowski.


## CI qualification

The completed [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42959340201) has only the test-line budget failure and its dependent gate. The official checker confirms that the exact baseline was already seven lines over its ceiling; this PR's added test lines are fully covered by its own allocation, leaving the same seven-line excess. Every other job in that run passed or was skipped. The baseline, tested merge tree and unchanged checker inputs were independently verified for the authorized inherited-failure landing route. No test was removed or allowance increased to absorb that debt.
